text:
B: Hello? Oh, hello. Can you hear me alright, love?
A: Yes, hello, good evening. I'm Tomasz.
B: Julie. Oh, I'm glad I got you, I was saying in the photo bit you looked very smart and tidy.
A: [laughs] Thank you. My wife irons the shirts, so I cannot take credit. You are Julie from the care home, yes? Somebody told me.
B: That's me! Gosh, word gets round, doesn't it. Yeah, senior care assistant, in Basingstoke. And you're the, erm, the buildings one?
A: Operations manager, facilities management. Office buildings, west London, Heathrow. Six site supervisors. Company car, but today I took the Central line. Terrible.
B: Oh, I don't know how you do the Tube. I went up for a show once and I was holding my bag like this the whole way.
A: [laughs] Yes, you have to. Er, the care work, it's hard, I think? Physically?
B: It is. My knees aren't what they were, and my back. I'd like to cut my hours down at about sixty-three, if the money'll let me. But I do love the residents. It's the ones without anyone that get to you, you know. Nobody visiting for months.
A: Yes. This I worry about. My father, he has heart condition, and he's in Poland, in Rzeszów. Three hours flying. Every time my sister calls in the evening, I think, okay, something happened.
B: Oh, love. That's hard, being so far. Has he got people round him?
A: My sister, yes, and my mother. But it's not the same, you know? Sorry, is that too much, what I said?
B: No, not at all, don't be daft. I think it's worse for the ones far away, honestly. When I had my mum, at least I could pop round. You go back much?
A: Every summer, every Christmas. And my daughter, Zofia, she's five, my father is crazy about her.
B: Oh, bless him. My grandchildren are the same with their grandad. My granddaughter's doing her nativity next week, she's a sheep. She's ever so proud.
A: [laughs] A sheep is important role.
B: That's what I told her! Better than a tree. What does Zofia like doing?
A: Swimming. Every Saturday I take her. She's not scared of anything in water, me, I'm standing at the edge like this.
B: [laughs] Oh, that's lovely, though, just the two of you. Them little things, that's what she'll remember, not the—
